     1	\section{Physical spatial pairings and the full occupation class}
     2	\label{S:spatial-occupation-foundation}
     3	
     4	Retain a nonzero original covariance from Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with its
     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =
     6	q-2a > 0$. The scalar $D$ is fixed. All profiles are real. The original positive
     7	temporal exponent and threshold imply $\alpha < 2$; this is the strict
     8	inequality used in the scalar powers and concavity. The finite variational value
     9	over nonnegative controls $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is that of
    10	Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
    11	
    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}
    34	
    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in
    38	its usual pointwise sense.
    39	
    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}
    41	  For every nonnegative nonzero $z \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$, let
    42	  \[
    43	    \lambda_z(c)^2=
    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
    46	  \]
    47	  This is positive and finite, and $\lambda_z$ is Lipschitz on every compact
    48	  positive $c$ interval. With the exact $M_a$
    49	  in~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-score}
    51	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
    52	    \lambda_z(1)-\frac{M_a}{2}B_\Gamma(z,z).
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{lemma}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  Choose nonnegative nonzero $f \in C_c^\infty(0,1)$ and $s_0 = 1/2$. Let
    58	  $k_f(s_0) = \int_0^1|s_0-t|^{-a}f(t)\ud t > 0$. The smooth test $\Psi(t,x) =
    59	  cf(t)z(x)/k_f(s_0)$ has mean $cU_z$ at $s_0$.
    60	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} gives boundedness of this
    61	  potential, the displayed real Rayleigh formula, and a positive rate for every
    62	  $c > 0$. Comparing identical unit tests makes $\lambda_z(c)^2$ Lipschitz with
    63	  constant $\|U_z\|_\infty$. On a positive compact interval its rate has a
    64	  positive floor by monotonicity, giving the square-root Lipschitz bound.
    65	
    66	  Use the nonincreasing smooth cutoff $\chi$ constructed in the proof of
    67	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}. For integers $n \ge 4$, set on
    68	  $(0,1)$
    69	  \[
    70	    f_n(t)=f_a(t)\chi(1/(nt))\chi(1/(n(1-t))),\qquad
    71	    k_n(s)=\int_0^1|s-t|^{-a}f_n(t)\ud t.
    72	  \]
    73	  Extend $f_n$ by zero. It is smooth compact, vanishes near both endpoints, is
    74	  nonzero, and increases to $f_a$. Thus, $\Psi_n = f_n\otimes z$ is a positive
    75	  smooth control. Monotone convergence
    76	  and~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-potential} give $k_n(s)\uparrow1$ for every
    77	  $s \in [0,1]$. Since the kernel is at least one on the unit square off its
    78	  null diagonal, $0 < c_0: = \int_0^1f_4 \le k_n(s) \le 1$. The mean is
    79	  $k_n(s)U_z$; hence its rate is $\lambda_z(k_n(s))$, converging to
    80	  $\lambda_z(1)$ and bounded by that finite number. Dominated convergence gives
    81	  $I_{\Psi_n} \to \lambda_z(1)$.
    82	
    83	  The Gaussian cost is exactly the nonnegative Tonelli pairing
    84	  \[
    85	    v_{\Psi_n}=B_\Gamma(z,z)\int_0^1f_n(s)k_n(s)\ud s.
    86	  \]
    87	  Its time integrand increases to $f_a$, so the cost tends to
    88	  $M_aB_\Gamma(z,z)$. The spatial factor is finite and positive: its smooth
    89	  compact autocorrelation is positive near zero, and homogeneity scales any
    90	  origin-centered ball of positive $\Gamma$ mass to every other positive radius.
    91	  Such a ball exists by exhaustion. Take the limit of the individual
    92	  inequalities $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} \ge I_{\Psi_n}-v_{\Psi_n}/2$. The variational
    93	  expression differences need not increase. No control depends on original large
    94	  time and no rough stochastic evolution has been used. This proves
    95	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls}.
    96	\end{proof}
    97	
    98	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
    99	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}
   100	  For real unit $g \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ put $R(g) =
   101	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is
   102	  a positive finite real number, and
   103	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-smooth-score}
   104	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
   105	    k\left[
   106	    \frac{R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}}{8M_aq^{q/2}}
   107	    \right]^{1/k}.
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	\end{proposition}
   110	
   111	\begin{proof}
   112	  The gradient energy $b(g)$ is positive: a nonzero $L^2$ function with zero
   113	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   114	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the
   115	  autocorrelation argument in the preceding proof gives $0 < A: =
   116	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) < \infty$. With $U_\ell g(x) = \ell^{d/2}g(\ell x)$, the
   117	  physical changes of variables give
   118	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   119	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   120	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).
   121	  \end{equation}
   122	  The factors in the first identity are $\ell^{2d}$ from the two squares,
   123	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.
   124	
   125	  For $\theta,\ell > 0$ choose the smooth control $z = \theta(U_\ell g)^2$. The
   126	  Rayleigh test $U_\ell g$ gives $\lambda_z(1)^2 \ge \theta\ell^\alpha
   127	  A-\ell^2b$, while $B_\Gamma(z,z) = \theta^2\ell^\alpha A$. For any $L > 0$,
   128	  put $u = \alpha/q > 0$ and choose
   129	  \[
   130	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   131	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).
   132	  \]
   133	  The radicand is $L^2$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} consequently
   134	  gives
   135	  \[
   136	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge L-CL^q,\qquad
   137	    C=\frac{M_a(1+u)^2}{2R(g)u^{\alpha/2}}>0.
   138	  \]
   139	  Its maximum occurs at $L^k = 1/(qC)$ and is $(k/q)(qC)^{-1/k}$. Since $1+u =
   140	  4/q$, $1/(q^qC) = R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}/(8M_aq^{q/2})$,
   141	  proving~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score}. The already finite
   142	  $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ bounds every ratio by
   143	  $8M_aq^{q/2}(S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}/k)^k/\alpha^{\alpha/2}$. A normalized compact
   144	  bump supplies a positive ratio. This proves positivity and finiteness of $R_0$
   145	  before any rough spatial extension is invoked. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}.
   147	\end{proof}
   148	
   149	\begin{proposition}[The physical four-linear extension]
   150	  \label{P:spatial-four-linear}
   151	  For real $f \in H^1(\R^d)$ define $N(f) = \|f\|_2^{1-\alpha/4}\|\nabla
   152	  f\|_2^{\alpha/4}$. Every physical square pairing is finite and
   153	  \begin{align}
   154	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)&\le R_0N(f)^4,\label{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}\\
   155	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   156	    &\le\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)A_{\mathrm{sp}}(h)}.
   157	    \label{E:spatial-square-CS}
   158	  \end{align}
   159	  The signed integral $C_4(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4) = B_\Gamma(f_1f_2,f_3f_4)$ is
   160	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with
   161	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-four-linear}
   162	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud\nu
   163	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).
   164	  \end{equation}
   165	  The ratio supremum $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ over all real unit $H^1$ profiles equals
   166	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.
   167	\end{proposition}
   168	
   169	\begin{proof}
   170	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   171	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   172	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   173	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   174	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   175	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   176	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   177	  convention gives
   178	  \[
   179	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   180	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   181	  \]
   182	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   183	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   184	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   185	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   186	  \[
   187	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   188	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   189	  \]
   190	  The squares of signed smooth profiles are already smooth and nonnegative.
   191	
   192	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   193	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   194	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   195	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   196	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   197	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   198	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   199	
   200	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   201	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   202	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   203	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   204	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   205	  continuity.
   206	
   207	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   208	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   209	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   210	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   211	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   212	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   213	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   214	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   215	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   216	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   217	
   218	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   219	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   220	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   221	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   222	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   223	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   224	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   225	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   226	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   227	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   228	\end{proof}
   229	
   230	\begin{proposition}[The spatial energy and static lower variational expression]
   231	  \label{P:spatial-energy-map}
   232	  Over all real unit $H^1$ profiles define the energy
   233	  \[
   234	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   235	    =\sup_{\|g\|_2=1}
   236	    \left(A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)-\frac{b(g)}2\right).
   237	  \]
   238	  Then
   239	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-energy-map}
   240	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   241	    =\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   242	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}^{2/(2-\alpha)}
   243	    \in(0,\infty).
   244	  \end{equation}
   245	  In particular,
   246	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   247	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}),
   248	    \qquad
   249	    F_0(z)=k\left[
   250	    \frac{(2z/(2-\alpha))^{(2-\alpha)/2}}{8q^{q/2}}
   251	    \right]^{1/k},\quad z>0.
   252	  \end{equation}
   253	  The subscript in $F_0$ labels this scalar map; the covariance retains its
   254	  original temporal exponent $a$.
   255	\end{proposition}
   256	
   257	\begin{proof}
   258	  Physical change of variables, or smooth approximation and
   259	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}, extends \eqref{E:spatial-dilation} to
   260	  real $H^1$ profiles. For fixed unit $g$, with $A,b > 0$, the maximum of
   261	  $\ell^\alpha A-\ell^2b/2$ occurs at $\ell^{2-\alpha} = \alpha A/b$ and equals
   262	  \[
   263	    \frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   264	    R(g)^{2/(2-\alpha)}.
   265	  \]
   266	  Dilation preserves the whole unit class and includes $\ell = 1$. Taking both
   267	  numerical suprema, then profiles with ratio tending to $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$,
   268	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. No optimizer is assumed. Smooth ratios
   269	  also approach $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   270	  Pass them through~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score} and substitute
   271	  \[
   272	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}\alpha^{\alpha/2}
   273	    =\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}}{2-\alpha}
   274	    \right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}.
   275	  \]
   276	  This gives~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}. This proves
   277	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-energy-map}.
   278	\end{proof}

   280	\subsection{The kernel row and full occupation energy}
   281	
   282	Define, for $u \ne 0$,
   283	\begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-damped-kernel}
   284	  K_\star(u)=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}
   285	  \int_0^\infty
   286	  e^{-(\lambda+\lambda^2/(2D))|u|}
   287	  \lambda^{a-1}\ud\lambda,
   288	\end{equation}
   289	and set $K_\star(0) = 0$ for time integration.
   290	
   291	\begin{lemma}[Exact row maximum]\label{L:occupation-kernel-row}
   292	  The kernel is even, positive off zero, locally integrable, decreasing on
   293	  $(0,\infty)$, and $K_\star(u) \le |u|^{-a}$ off zero. Its exact row maximum on
   294	  $[0,1]$ is
   295	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-kernel-row}
   296	    \max_{s\in[0,1]}\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud t
   297	    =R_\star:=2\int_0^{1/2}K_\star(u)\ud u\in(0,\infty).
   298	  \end{equation}
   299	\end{lemma}
   300	
   301	\begin{proof}
   302	  Dropping the positive quadratic damping bounds the mixture by the Gamma
   303	  integral $|u|^{-a}$. Positivity and monotonicity follow directly from the
   304	  integrand, and $a < 1$ gives local integrability. Put $\Phi(t) =
   305	  \int_0^tK_\star(u)\ud u$. It is concave because its integrand is decreasing on
   306	  positive arguments. The row is $\Phi(s)+\Phi(1-s) \le 2\Phi(1/2)$, with
   307	  equality at $s = 1/2$. The diagonal value changes no time integral. This
   308	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-kernel-row}.
   309	\end{proof}
   310	
   311	Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the full class of strongly $H^1(\R^d;\R)$-measurable fields
   312	$s\mapsto g_s$ on $(0,1)$ with $\|g_s\|_2 = 1$ a.e. and $T(g) =
   313	\int_0^1b(g_s)\ud s < \infty$. No time smoothness, common compact support or
   314	optimizer condition is imposed.
   315	
   316	\begin{proposition}[The full physical occupation class]
   317	  \label{P:occupation-physical-class}
   318	  The pairings $(s,t)\mapsto B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)$ are measurable,
   319	  representative independent and equal to their physical integrals. With
   320	  \[
   321	    J(g)=\int_0^1\int_0^1
   322	    K_\star(s-t)B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)\ud s\ud t,
   323	  \]
   324	  every $g \in \mathcal{O}$ satisfies
   325	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-physical-bound}
   326	    0\le J(g)\le R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty.
   327	  \end{equation}
   328	  The energy over exactly this full class satisfies
   329	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-own-energy}
   330	    0<\mathcal{E}_\star^{\mathcal{O}}
   331	    :=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\big(J(g)-T(g)/2\big)
   332	    \le R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty.

  3255	## SpatialStaticControls (whole result)
  3256	
  3257	Formalizes `L:spatial-static-controls` (Smooth temporal controls) of the
  3258	section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
  3259	(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `975feb3`): statement lines
  3260	40-54 (the definition of `lambda_z(c)^2`, lines 42-46; the display
  3261	`E:spatial-static-score`, lines 50-53), proof lines 56-96. The section's
  3262	standing assumptions (lines 4-10) are a nonzero covariance from `H:homog`
  3263	and `a = alpha0`; `U_z = Gamma * z` pointwise for smooth compact `z` (lines
  3264	37-38). The wrappers carry `HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and
  3265	`Gamma != 0`, and use the exponent `alpha0`.
  3266	
  3267	Objects. `lamSq U c` is `sSup` of the real Rayleigh set
  3268	(`WeakSobolev.rayleighSet`) of the potential `c U`, that is the supremum of
  3269	`c int U g^2 - ||grad g||_2^2` over unit `g` in `H^1(R^d;R)` (weak
  3270	gradients); `lam U c = sqrt (lamSq U c)` and `lamZ Gamma z = lam (Gamma * z)`
  3271	is `lambda_z`. The definition is the TeX's display with a general potential;
  3272	for the bounded potentials used here the side condition of
  3273	`WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is automatic (`isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded`),
  3274	so the set is the manuscript's set. `I_Psi` and `v_Psi` are the package's
  3275	`VariationalDilation.integratedRate` (the integral of the real-Rayleigh rate)
  3276	and `VariationalDilation.rawCost` (the integral form of the cost); their
  3277	identification with `sqrt(-E_s)` and `E W(Psi)^2` (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`,
  3278	`L:compact-raw-profile`) stays outside Lean, as for `VariationalDilation`.
  3279	`B_Gamma(z,z)` is `OccupationKernelRow.pairing` (the extended nonnegative
  3280	integral of `E:spatial-physical-pair`) at `zE z = ofReal o z`;
  3281	`pairing_bridge` proves it finite and equal to `ofReal (int z U_z)`, and the
  3282	statements use its `toReal` only after that. `M_a` is
  3283	`TemporalEquilibrium.mass` (`E:temporal-equilibrium-mass`) and `f_a` is
  3284	`TemporalEquilibrium.density`.
  3285	
  3286	Part (i). `spatial_static_controls_rate_paper` proves, for a nonnegative
  3287	nonzero test function `z`: every `y -> z(x-y)` is `Gamma`-integrable; for
  3288	`c > 0` the Rayleigh set of `c U_z` is nonempty and bounded above (so
  3289	`lambda_z(c)^2` is a finite supremum), `0 < lambda_z(c)^2`, `0 < lambda_z(c)`;
  3290	and `lambda_z` is Lipschitz on every `[c_1, c_2]` with `c_1 > 0`. The general
  3291	form `static_rate` also gives `|lambda_z(c)^2 - lambda_z(c')^2| <= M |c - c'|`
  3292	for every upper bound `M` of `U_z` (the TeX's constant `||U_z||_inf`, lines
  3293	62-63) without any floor. Positivity rests on the named input
  3294	`RayleighFloor Gamma`: for every nonnegative nonzero test function `z`, the
  3295	Rayleigh set of `U_z` contains a positive value. It stands for the dilation
  3296	floor lemma of wave item L6-d at `V = Gamma * z`
  3297	(`VariationalFloor.rayleighSet_floor`); it is discharged under the section's
  3298	hypotheses in `SpatialOccupationCompleted` (`rayleighFloor_of_homog`, with the
  3299	completed wrapper `spatial_static_controls_completed_paper`). Disclosure: since `U_z` is bounded (proved here), this input
  3300	is equivalent to `lambda_z(1)^2 > 0` for every such `z`, that is to the
  3301	positivity claim of part (i) itself; the Lean content of part (i) beyond the
  3302	input is the finiteness, the transfer of positivity to every `c > 0` (through
  3303	`Gamma * (c z) = c U_z`) and the Lipschitz bounds. The TeX's positivity route
  3304	is different: a positive rate of a smooth test with mean `c U_z` through
  3305	`P:variational-unmasked-rate` and `P:compact-original-common-trial` (lines
  3306	57-62). The input is satisfiable (`rayleighFloor_volume`: white noise,
  3307	`Gamma` = Lebesgue measure) and fails for `Gamma = 0` (refutation
  3308	`FloorZeroCovariance`). The boundedness of `U_z` comes from the Gaussian
  3309	envelope (`VariationalMean.conv_le`), not from `P:variational-unmasked-rate`
  3310	as in the TeX (lines 60-61).
  3311	
  3312	Part (ii). `spatial_static_score_paper` states `E:spatial-static-score` in
  3313	the existential form (the owner's decision 2 of wave L6): `B_Gamma(z,z)` is
  3314	finite, the Rayleigh set defining `lambda_z(1)` is nonempty and bounded
  3315	above, and every `y < lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z)` is exceeded by
  3316	`I_Psi - v_Psi/2` for some `Psi` in `C_pos` whose rate and time cost
  3317	integrand are integrable on `(0,1)`. This is equivalent to the TeX display
  3318	whenever `S_1^pos` is a finite supremum; `spatial_static_score_sSup_paper`
  3319	gives the display itself, `lambda_z(1) - (M_a/2) B_Gamma(z,z) <= S_1^pos`, on
  3320	the named input `VariationalRate.S1Bdd alpha0 Gamma` (boundedness above of
  3321	`VariationalRate.score1Set`, that is of
  3322	`{I_Psi - v_Psi/2 : Psi in C_pos}`, word for word the boundedness claim of
  3323	`P:variational-positive-scores`, `integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines
  3324	272-274, whose manuscript proof, lines 309-325, uses `T:full-upper`). Part
  3325	(ii) uses neither the floor nor `Gamma != 0`. The proof follows the TeX:
  3326	`Psi_n = f_n (x) z` (`ctrl`, in `C_pos` by `ctrl_mem`), mean
  3327	`k_n(s) U_z` (`mean_ctrl`), rate `lambda_z(k_n(s))` (`rate_ctrl`), cost
  3328	`(int_0^1 f_n k_n) int z U_z` (`rawCost_ctrl`), `k_n -> 1` with
  3329	`0 <= k_n <= 1` (`E:temporal-equilibrium-potential` via
  3330	`TemporalEquilibrium.potential_eq_one`), `int f_n k_n -> M_a`, and the
  3331	limit of the scores (`score_tendsto`); `ctrl_genuine` shows that every
  3332	Rayleigh set of `Psi_n` is nonempty and bounded and every integrand is
  3333	integrable, so no score is a junk value.
  3334	
  3335	Two bridges connect this module to `P:spatial-smooth-ratio`:
  3336	`pairing_eq_spatialPair` proves that the extended pairing
  3337	`OccupationKernelRow.pairing` and the real iterated integral
  3338	`SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair` agree (and are finite) for continuous,
  3339	nonnegative, compactly supported functions and locally finite `Gamma`, and
  3340	`isUnitH1_of_unitTest` shows that a real unit test of `SpatialFourierBound`
  3341	with its classical gradient is a unit `H^1` pair. The weak gradient of a test
  3342	function (`VariationalFloor.hasWeakGradient_of_test`), the radius lemma
  3343	(`VariationalFloor.exists_radius_fn`) and the score set, `S1Bdd`, `S1pos`
  3344	(`VariationalRate`) are shared with other modules and documented there.
  3345

3346	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: local finiteness of `Gamma` (`Gamma_radon`,
  3347	for Tonelli in `B_Gamma`); integrability of every integrand; nonemptiness and
  3348	boundedness of every Rayleigh set whose supremum is used; finiteness of
  3349	`B_Gamma(z,z)` before `toReal`. Hypotheses carried but unused: `Gamma != 0` in
  3350	both wrappers (part (i) relies on it only through `RayleighFloor`), and the
  3351	fields of `H:homog` other than `Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered`, `spectral`,
  3352	`Gamma_radon`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`.
  3353	
  3354	Proof-route differences: (1) the cutoff is
  3355	`cut_n(t) = smoothTransition((n+4)t - 1) smoothTransition((n+4)(1-t) - 1)`
  3356	instead of `chi(1/(nt)) chi(1/(n(1-t)))` (lines 66-72); `fn = f_a cut_n`
  3357	has the properties the proof uses (smooth, vanishing near the endpoints,
  3358	nonzero, `0 <= f_n <= f_a`, `f_n -> f_a`); monotonicity in `n` is not proved
  3359	or used; (2) dominated convergence replaces the monotone convergence of
  3360	lines 75-77 and 87-88; (3) the TeX's floor `c_0 <= k_n(s)` (line 78) is not
  3361	needed, because `lambda_z^2` is globally Lipschitz and `lambda_z` therefore
  3362	continuous on `R` (`lam_continuous`); (4) the mean and cost of `f_n (x) z` are
  3363	unconditional identities of Bochner integrals. Not formalized: the positivity
  3364	of `B_Gamma(z,z)` (lines 88-91), which the stated bound does not need; the
  3365	identifications of `lambda`, `I_Psi`, `v_Psi` named above; the finiteness of
  3366	`S_1^pos` (the named input `S1Bdd`). Constant potentials
  3367	(`rayleighSet_const`, `lamSq_const`) support the satisfiability check and
  3368	the refutations (`refutations/spatial-static-controls/`: the floor fails for
  3369	`Gamma = 0`, the Lipschitz constant `M/2` is false, `lambda` is not
  3370	Lipschitz on `[0,1]`, positivity fails for `z = 0`).

   132	/-- A unit `H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)` pair: `f ∈ L²` with `‖f‖₂ = 1` and an `L²` weak
   133	gradient `g`.  These are the trials of `E:variational-real-rayleigh` without the
   134	potential side condition. -/
   135	def IsUnitH1 (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : Prop :=
   136	  MemLp f 2 volume ∧ MemLp g 2 volume ∧ HasWeakGradient f g ∧ ∫ x, f x ^ 2 = 1
   137	
   138	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  A test function with `∫ f² = 1` and its
   139	classical gradient form a unit `H^1` pair. -/
   140	theorem isUnitH1_of_test {f : Rd d → ℝ} (hf : IsTestFunction f) (hu : ∫ x, f x ^ 2 = 1) :
   141	    IsUnitH1 f (fun x => (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Rd d)).symm (fderiv ℝ f x)) := by
   142	  refine ⟨hf.1.continuous.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport hf.2, ?_,
   143	    VariationalFloor.hasWeakGradient_of_test hf, hu⟩
   144	  have hc : Continuous fun x => (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Rd d)).symm (fderiv ℝ f x) :=
   145	    (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Rd d)).symm.continuous.comp
   146	      (hf.1.continuous_fderiv (by simp))
   147	  refine hc.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport ?_
   148	  exact (hf.2.fderiv ℝ).comp_left (by simp)

   150	/-- The connection between the two unit-profile predicates of the package: a
   151	real unit test `g ∈ C_c^∞` (`SpatialFourierBound.IsUnitTest`, the profiles of
   152	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio`) with its classical gradient `VariationalFloor.grad g`
   153	is a unit `H^1` pair (`IsUnitH1`, the trials of the Rayleigh sets here). -/
   154	theorem isUnitH1_of_unitTest {g : Rd d → ℝ} (hg : SpatialFourierBound.IsUnitTest g) :
   155	    IsUnitH1 g (VariationalFloor.grad g) :=
   156	  isUnitH1_of_test ⟨hg.1, hg.2.1⟩ hg.2.2
   157	
   158	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Unit `H^1` pairs exist (a normalized
   159	smooth bump). -/
   160	theorem exists_isUnitH1 : ∃ f : Rd d → ℝ, ∃ g : Rd d → Rd d, IsUnitH1 f g := by
   161	  let b : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d) := ⟨1, 2, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩
   162	  have hb0 : (b : Rd d → ℝ) 0 = 1 :=
   163	    b.one_of_mem_closedBall (Metric.mem_closedBall_self (by norm_num))
   164	  set I : ℝ := ∫ x, (b : Rd d → ℝ) x ^ 2 with hIdef
   165	  have hI : 0 < I := by
   166	    refine Continuous.integral_pos_of_hasCompactSupport_nonneg_nonzero (x := 0)
   167	      (b.continuous.pow 2) (b.hasCompactSupport.comp_left (g := fun t : ℝ => t ^ 2) (by norm_num))
   168	      (fun x => sq_nonneg _) ?_
   169	    simp [hb0]
   170	  set c : ℝ := (Real.sqrt I)⁻¹ with hcdef
   171	  let f : Rd d → ℝ := fun x => c * (b : Rd d → ℝ) x
   172	  have hf : IsTestFunction f := ⟨contDiff_const.mul b.contDiff, b.hasCompactSupport.mul_left⟩
   173	  have hu : ∫ x, f x ^ 2 = 1 := by
   174	    have e : ∀ x, f x ^ 2 = c ^ 2 * (b : Rd d → ℝ) x ^ 2 := fun x => by simp only [f]; ring
   175	    simp_rw [e]
   176	    rw [integral_const_mul, ← hIdef, hcdef, inv_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hI.le, inv_mul_cancel₀ hI.ne']
   177	  exact ⟨f, _, isUnitH1_of_test hf hu⟩

   180	variable {V : Rd d → ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hVc : Continuous V) (hVM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M)
   181	include hVc hVM
   182	
   183	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  For a continuous bounded potential the side condition of
   184	`WeakSobolev.IsRayleighTrial` is automatic: the trials are exactly the unit
   185	`H^1` pairs. -/
   186	theorem isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) :
   187	    IsRayleighTrial V f g ↔ IsUnitH1 f g := by
   188	  constructor
   189	  · intro h; exact ⟨h.memLp_f, h.memLp_g, h.weakGrad, h.unit⟩
   190	  · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩
   191	    exact ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, VariationalMean.integrable_pot_of_bounded hVc hVM h1⟩
   192	
   193	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.
   194	For a continuous bounded potential the real Rayleigh set is nonempty. -/
   195	theorem rayleighSet_nonempty_of_bounded : (rayleighSet V).Nonempty := by
   196	  obtain ⟨f, g, h⟩ := exists_isUnitH1 (d := d)
   197	  exact ⟨_, f, g, (isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded hVc hVM f g).2 h, rfl⟩
   198	
   199	end bounded
   200	
   201	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  `∫ V f² ≤ M` for a trial with `V ≤ M`. -/
   202	theorem integral_pot_le {V : Rd d → ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hVM : ∀ x, V x ≤ M) {f : Rd d → ℝ}
   203	    {g : Rd d → Rd d} (h : IsRayleighTrial V f g) : ∫ x, V x * f x ^ 2 ≤ M := by
   204	  calc ∫ x, V x * f x ^ 2 ≤ ∫ x, M * f x ^ 2 :=
   205	        integral_mono h.integrable_pot (h.memLp_f.integrable_sq.const_mul M)
   206	          fun x => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hVM x) (sq_nonneg _)
   207	    _ = M := by rw [integral_const_mul, h.unit, mul_one]
   208	
   209	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Every Rayleigh value is at most `M`
   210	when `V ≤ M`; so the Rayleigh set is bounded above. -/
   211	theorem rayleighValue_le {V : Rd d → ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hVM : ∀ x, V x ≤ M) {f : Rd d → ℝ}
   212	    {g : Rd d → Rd d} (h : IsRayleighTrial V f g) : rayleighValue V f g ≤ M := by
   213	  have h1 := integral_pot_le hVM h
   214	  have h2 : 0 ≤ ∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2 := integral_nonneg fun _ => sq_nonneg _
   215	  unfold rayleighValue; linarith
   216	
   217	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  `BddAbove (rayleighSet V)` for `V ≤ M`. -/
   218	theorem rayleighSet_bddAbove {V : Rd d → ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hVM : ∀ x, V x ≤ M) :
   219	    BddAbove (rayleighSet V) := by
   220	  refine ⟨M, ?_⟩
   221	  rintro q ⟨f, g, h, rfl⟩
   222	  exact rayleighValue_le hVM h
   223	
   224	/-! ### The squared rate `λ_U(c)²` and the rate `λ_U(c)` -/
   225	
   226	/-- `λ_U(c)² = sup{c ∫ U g² - ‖∇g‖₂² : g ∈ H^1(ℝ^d;ℝ), ‖g‖₂ = 1}` (the
   227	displayed definition of `L:spatial-static-controls`, TeX lines 42-46, with a
   228	general potential `U`; the manuscript's case is `U = U_z = Γ * z`). -/
   229	def lamSq (U : Rd d → ℝ) (c : ℝ) : ℝ := sSup (rayleighSet (fun x => c * U x))
   230	
   231	/-- `λ_U(c) = √(λ_U(c)²)` (`WeakSobolev.rayleighRate` of the potential `c U`). -/
   232	def lam (U : Rd d → ℝ) (c : ℝ) : ℝ := rayleighRate (fun x => c * U x)
   233	
   234	theorem lam_eq_sqrt (U : Rd d → ℝ) (c : ℝ) : lam U c = Real.sqrt (lamSq U c) := rfl
   235	
   236	section potential
   237	variable {U : Rd d → ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hUc : Continuous U) (hU0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ U x) (hUM : ∀ x, U x ≤ M)
   238	include hUc hU0 hUM
   239	
   240	omit hUc in
   241	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  `M ≥ 0`. -/
   242	theorem bound_nonneg : 0 ≤ M := (hU0 0).trans (hUM 0)
   243	
   244	omit hUc in
   245	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  `|c U| ≤ |c| M`. -/
   246	theorem abs_cU_le (c : ℝ) (x : Rd d) : |c * U x| ≤ |c| * M := by
   247	  rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (hU0 x)]
   248	  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hUM x) (abs_nonneg c)
   249	
   250	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.
   251	The trials of `c U` are the unit `H^1` pairs, for every real `c`. -/
   252	theorem trial_cU_iff (c : ℝ) (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) :
   253	    IsRayleighTrial (fun x => c * U x) f g ↔ IsUnitH1 f g :=
   254	  isRayleighTrial_iff_of_bounded (continuous_const.mul hUc)
   255	    (abs_cU_le hU0 hUM c) f g
   256	
   257	omit hUc hU0 hUM in
   258	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  The Rayleigh value of `c U` is
   259	`c ∫ U f² - ∫ ‖g‖²`. -/
   260	theorem value_cU {c : ℝ} {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d} :
   261	    rayleighValue (fun x => c * U x) f g = c * (∫ x, U x * f x ^ 2) - ∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2 := by
   262	  unfold rayleighValue
   263	  rw [← integral_const_mul]
   264	  congr 2; funext x; ring
   265	
   266	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  `0 ≤ ∫ U f² ≤ M` on unit pairs. -/
   267	theorem integral_U_mem {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d} (h : IsUnitH1 f g) :
   268	    0 ≤ ∫ x, U x * f x ^ 2 ∧ ∫ x, U x * f x ^ 2 ≤ M := by
   269	  have hT : IsRayleighTrial (fun x => 1 * U x) f g := (trial_cU_iff hUc hU0 hUM 1 f g).2 h
   270	  refine ⟨integral_nonneg fun x => mul_nonneg (hU0 x) (sq_nonneg _), ?_⟩
   271	  have := integral_pot_le (V := fun x => 1 * U x) (M := M) (fun x => by simpa using hUM x) hT
   272	  simpa using this
   273	
   274	/-- The Rayleigh set of `c U` is nonempty. -/
   275	theorem cU_nonempty (c : ℝ) : (rayleighSet (fun x => c * U x)).Nonempty := by
   276	  obtain ⟨f, g, h⟩ := exists_isUnitH1 (d := d)
   277	  exact ⟨_, f, g, (trial_cU_iff hUc hU0 hUM c f g).2 h, rfl⟩
   278	
   279	omit hUc in
   280	/-- The Rayleigh set of `c U` is bounded above by `|c| M`. -/
   281	theorem cU_bddAbove (c : ℝ) : BddAbove (rayleighSet (fun x => c * U x)) :=
   282	  rayleighSet_bddAbove (M := |c| * M) fun x => (le_abs_self _).trans (abs_cU_le hU0 hUM c x)
   283	
   284	/-- `λ_U(c)² ≤ |c| M` (finiteness, TeX line 47). -/
   285	theorem lamSq_le (c : ℝ) : lamSq U c ≤ |c| * M := by
   286	  refine csSup_le (cU_nonempty hUc hU0 hUM c) ?_
   287	  rintro q ⟨f, g, h, rfl⟩
   288	  exact rayleighValue_le (fun x => (le_abs_self _).trans (abs_cU_le hU0 hUM c x)) h
   289	
   290	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Comparing identical unit tests:
   291	`λ_U(c)² ≤ λ_U(c')² + |c - c'| M` (TeX lines 62-63). -/
   292	theorem lamSq_le_add (c c' : ℝ) : lamSq U c ≤ lamSq U c' + |c - c'| * M := by
   293	  refine csSup_le (cU_nonempty hUc hU0 hUM c) ?_
   294	  rintro q ⟨f, g, h, rfl⟩
   295	  have hu := (trial_cU_iff hUc hU0 hUM c f g).1 h
   296	  have h' := (trial_cU_iff hUc hU0 hUM c' f g).2 hu
   297	  have hq' : rayleighValue (fun x => c' * U x) f g ≤ lamSq U c' :=
   298	    le_csSup (cU_bddAbove hU0 hUM c') ⟨f, g, h', rfl⟩
   299	  obtain ⟨i0, i1⟩ := integral_U_mem hUc hU0 hUM hu
   300	  rw [value_cU] at hq' ⊢

301	  have : (c - c') * ∫ x, U x * f x ^ 2 ≤ |c - c'| * M :=
   302	    (le_abs_self _).trans (by
   303	      rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg i0]
   304	      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left i1 (abs_nonneg _))
   305	  nlinarith
   306	
   307	/-- `c ↦ λ_U(c)²` is Lipschitz with constant `M = sup U` on all of `ℝ`
   308	(TeX lines 62-63: "comparing identical unit tests makes `λ_z(c)²` Lipschitz
   309	with constant `‖U_z‖_∞`"). -/
   310	theorem lamSq_lip (c c' : ℝ) : |lamSq U c - lamSq U c'| ≤ M * |c - c'| := by
   311	  rw [abs_sub_le_iff]
   312	  have h1 := lamSq_le_add hUc hU0 hUM c c'
   313	  have h2 := lamSq_le_add hUc hU0 hUM c' c
   314	  rw [abs_sub_comm] at h2
   315	  constructor <;> linarith
   316	
   317	/-- `c ↦ λ_U(c)²` is nondecreasing (`U ≥ 0`). -/
   318	theorem lamSq_mono {c c' : ℝ} (hcc : c ≤ c') : lamSq U c ≤ lamSq U c' := by
   319	  refine csSup_le (cU_nonempty hUc hU0 hUM c) ?_
   320	  rintro q ⟨f, g, h, rfl⟩
   321	  have hu := (trial_cU_iff hUc hU0 hUM c f g).1 h
   322	  have h' := (trial_cU_iff hUc hU0 hUM c' f g).2 hu
   323	  refine le_trans ?_ (le_csSup (cU_bddAbove hU0 hUM c') ⟨f, g, h', rfl⟩)
   324	  rw [value_cU, value_cU]
   325	  have := (integral_U_mem hUc hU0 hUM hu).1
   326	  nlinarith
   327	
   328	/-- `c ↦ λ_U(c)` is nondecreasing. -/
   329	theorem lam_mono {c c' : ℝ} (hcc : c ≤ c') : lam U c ≤ lam U c' :=
   330	  Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (lamSq_mono hUc hU0 hUM hcc)
   331	
   332	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  `c ↦ λ_U(c)` is continuous on `ℝ`. -/
   333	theorem lam_continuous : Continuous (lam U) := by
   334	  have hM := bound_nonneg hU0 hUM
   335	  have hL : LipschitzWith (Real.toNNReal M) (lamSq U) :=
   336	    LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul fun c c' => by
   337	      rw [Real.dist_eq, Real.dist_eq, Real.coe_toNNReal _ hM]
   338	      exact lamSq_lip hUc hU0 hUM c c'
   339	  exact Real.continuous_sqrt.comp hL.continuous
   340	
   341	/-- Lipschitz bound of `λ_U` on `[c₁, c₂]` from a positive floor
   342	`λ_U(c₁)² > 0` (TeX lines 63-64: "on a positive compact interval its rate has a
   343	positive floor by monotonicity, giving the square-root Lipschitz bound"). -/
   344	theorem lam_lipschitzOn {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < lamSq U c₁) :
   345	    ∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzOnWith K (lam U) (Icc c₁ c₂) := by
   346	  have hM := bound_nonneg hU0 hUM
   347	  set m := Real.sqrt (lamSq U c₁) with hmdef
   348	  have hm : 0 < m := Real.sqrt_pos.2 hpos
   349	  refine ⟨Real.toNNReal (M / (2 * m)), LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul fun c hc c' hc' => ?_⟩
   350	  rw [Real.dist_eq, Real.dist_eq, Real.coe_toNNReal _ (by positivity), lam_eq_sqrt,
   351	    lam_eq_sqrt]
   352	  have hA : lamSq U c₁ ≤ lamSq U c := lamSq_mono hUc hU0 hUM hc.1
   353	  have hB : lamSq U c₁ ≤ lamSq U c' := lamSq_mono hUc hU0 hUM hc'.1
   354	  have sA : m ≤ Real.sqrt (lamSq U c) := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hA
   355	  have sB : m ≤ Real.sqrt (lamSq U c') := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hB
   356	  have qA := Real.sq_sqrt (hpos.le.trans hA)
   357	  have qB := Real.sq_sqrt (hpos.le.trans hB)
   358	  set p := Real.sqrt (lamSq U c)
   359	  set q := Real.sqrt (lamSq U c')
   360	  have hsum : 0 < p + q := by linarith
   361	  have key : |p - q| * (p + q) = |lamSq U c - lamSq U c'| := by
   362	    rw [← abs_of_pos hsum, ← abs_mul]
   363	    congr 1
   364	    rw [← qA, ← qB]; ring
   365	  have hlip := lamSq_lip hUc hU0 hUM c c'
   366	  have h2m : 2 * m ≤ p + q := by linarith
   367	  rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
   368	  calc |p - q| * (2 * m) ≤ |p - q| * (p + q) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h2m (abs_nonneg _)
   369	    _ ≤ M * |c - c'| := key ▸ hlip
   370	
   371	end potential

   373	/-! ### The potential `U_z = Γ * z` and the positivity floor -/
   374	
   375	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  `Γ * (c z) = c (Γ * z)` (unconditional
   376	identity of Bochner integrals). -/
   377	theorem conv_const_mul (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (z : Rd d → ℝ) (c : ℝ) :
   378	    conv Γ (fun y => c * z y) = fun x => c * conv Γ z x :=
   379	  funext fun _ => integral_const_mul c _
   380	
   381	/-- For a nonnegative test function `z`, a tempered `Γ`, `μ` with the spectral
   382	convention: `y ↦ z(x-y)` is `Γ`-integrable for every `x` (so `U_z(x)` is a
   383	genuine integral), `U_z = Γ * z` is continuous, nonnegative and bounded above
   384	(TeX lines 60-61 use this boundedness, through `P:variational-unmasked-rate`,
   385	which the TeX quotes for "boundedness of this potential"; here it comes from
   386	`VariationalMean.conv_le`, the Gaussian envelope). -/
   387	theorem convZ_props {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓt : IsTempered Γ) (hμt : IsTempered μ)
   388	    (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) {z : Rd d → ℝ} (hz : IsTestFunction z)
   389	    (hz0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ z x) :
   390	    (∀ x, Integrable (fun y => z (x - y)) Γ) ∧ Continuous (conv Γ z) ∧
   391	      (∀ x, 0 ≤ conv Γ z x) ∧ ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ x, conv Γ z x ≤ M := by
   392	  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := hz.1.continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support hz.2
   393	  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport (𝕂 := ℝ) hz.2 hz.1 (by simp)
   394	  obtain ⟨R, -, hR⟩ := VariationalFloor.exists_radius_fn hz.2
   395	  set Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ := fun p => z p.2 with hΨdef
   396	  have hΨc : Continuous Ψ := hz.1.continuous.comp continuous_snd
   397	  have hΨB : ∀ p, |Ψ p| ≤ B := fun p => by simpa [Ψ] using hB p.2
   398	  have hΨL : ∀ p q, |Ψ p - Ψ q| ≤ (L : ℝ) * dist p q := fun p q => by
   399	    have h1 := hL.dist_le_mul p.2 q.2
   400	    rw [Real.dist_eq] at h1
   401	    have h2 : dist p.2 q.2 ≤ dist p q := by rw [Prod.dist_eq]; exact le_max_right _ _
   402	    exact h1.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h2 L.2)
   403	  have hΨR : ∀ u y, R < ‖y‖ → Ψ (u, y) = 0 := fun u y hy => hR y hy
   404	  refine ⟨fun x => VariationalMean.conv_integrable hΓt hμt hsp hΨc hΨB hΨR 0 x, ?_,
   405	    fun x => integral_nonneg fun y => hz0 _, ⟨B * Real.exp (R ^ 2 / 2) * VariationalMean.gMass Γ,
   406	      fun x => le_of_abs_le (VariationalMean.conv_le hΓt hμt hsp hΨB hΨR 0 x)⟩⟩
   407	  have := (VariationalMean.convT_continuous hΓt hμt hsp hΨc hΨB hΨL hΨR).comp
   408	    (continuous_const.prodMk continuous_id : Continuous fun x : Rd d => ((0 : ℝ), x))
   409	  exact this
   410	
   411	/-- The positivity floor, taken as a named input: the dilation floor lemma of
   412	wave item L6-d at the potential `V = Γ * z`.  For every nonnegative, nonzero
   413	test function `z`, the real Rayleigh set of `U_z = Γ * z` contains a positive
   414	value.  For `U_z` bounded this says exactly that the Rayleigh supremum of `U_z`
   415	is positive.  The manuscript asserts this for every nonzero `Γ` satisfying
   416	`H:homog` (the L6-d route uses `α < 2`); it is not proved here.  It holds for
   417	white noise (`rayleighFloor_volume`) and fails for `Γ = 0`. -/
   418	def RayleighFloor (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
   419	  ∀ z : Rd d → ℝ, IsTestFunction z → (∀ x, 0 ≤ z x) → z ≠ 0 →
   420	    ∃ q ∈ rayleighSet (conv Γ z), 0 < q
   421	
   422	/-- `λ_z(c) = λ_{U_z}(c)` with `U_z = Γ * z` (TeX lines 42-46). -/
   423	def lamZ (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (z : Rd d → ℝ) (c : ℝ) : ℝ := lam (conv Γ z) c
   424	
   425	/-- Part (i) of `L:spatial-static-controls` (TeX lines 41-49), general form
   426	(tempered `Γ`, `μ`, spectral convention, the floor `RayleighFloor Γ`), for a
   427	nonnegative nonzero test function `z`: (a) for every real `c` the Rayleigh set
   428	of `c U_z` is nonempty and bounded above; (b) for `c > 0`, `λ_z(c)² > 0`,
   429	`λ_z(c) > 0` and `λ_z(c)² = (√·)²`; (c) for every upper bound `M` of `U_z`
   430	(in particular `‖U_z‖_∞`), `|λ_z(c)² - λ_z(c')²| ≤ M |c - c'|`, and such an `M`
   431	exists; (d) `λ_z` is Lipschitz on every compact positive interval
   432	`[c₁, c₂]`, `c₁ > 0`.  The floor is used only for (b) and (d). -/
   433	theorem static_rate {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓt : IsTempered Γ) (hμt : IsTempered μ)
   434	    (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) (hfloor : RayleighFloor Γ) {z : Rd d → ℝ}
   435	    (hz : IsTestFunction z) (hz0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ z x) (hzne : z ≠ 0) :
   436	    (∀ c : ℝ, (rayleighSet (fun x => c * conv Γ z x)).Nonempty ∧
   437	      BddAbove (rayleighSet (fun x => c * conv Γ z x))) ∧
   438	    (∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → 0 < lamSq (conv Γ z) c ∧ 0 < lamZ Γ z c ∧
   439	      lamZ Γ z c ^ 2 = lamSq (conv Γ z) c) ∧
   440	    (∃ M : ℝ, ∀ x, conv Γ z x ≤ M) ∧
   441	    (∀ M : ℝ, (∀ x, conv Γ z x ≤ M) → ∀ c c' : ℝ,
   442	      |lamSq (conv Γ z) c - lamSq (conv Γ z) c'| ≤ M * |c - c'|) ∧
   443	    (∀ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ → ∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzOnWith K (lamZ Γ z) (Icc c₁ c₂)) := by
   444	  obtain ⟨-, hUc, hU0, ⟨M, hUM⟩⟩ := convZ_props hΓt hμt hsp hz hz0
   445	  have hpos : ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → 0 < lamSq (conv Γ z) c := by
   446	    intro c hc
   447	    have hzc : IsTestFunction (fun y => c * z y) := ⟨contDiff_const.mul hz.1, hz.2.mul_left⟩
   448	    have hne : (fun y => c * z y) ≠ 0 := by
   449	      intro h; apply hzne; funext y
   450	      have := congrFun h y
   451	      simpa [hc.ne'] using this
   452	    obtain ⟨q, hq, hq0⟩ := hfloor _ hzc (fun y => mul_nonneg hc.le (hz0 y)) hne
   453	    rw [conv_const_mul] at hq
   454	    exact hq0.trans_le (le_csSup (cU_bddAbove hU0 hUM c) hq)
   455	  refine ⟨fun c => ⟨cU_nonempty hUc hU0 hUM c, cU_bddAbove hU0 hUM c⟩, fun c hc => ?_,
   456	    ⟨M, hUM⟩, fun M' hM' c c' => lamSq_lip hUc hU0 hM' c c', fun c₁ c₂ hc₁ =>
   457	      lam_lipschitzOn hUc hU0 hUM (hpos c₁ hc₁)⟩
   458	  have h := hpos c hc
   459	  exact ⟨h, Real.sqrt_pos.2 h, Real.sq_sqrt h.le⟩
   460	
   461	/-! ### The temporal cutoffs `f_n` -/
   462	
   463	/-- The smooth cutoff `cut_n(t) = χ̃((n+4)t - 1) χ̃((n+4)(1-t) - 1)` with
   464	`χ̃ = Real.smoothTransition` (`0` on `(-∞,0]`, `1` on `[1,∞)`).  Lean route: it
   465	replaces the manuscript's `χ(1/(nt)) χ(1/(n(1-t)))` (TeX lines 66-72; `χ` from
   466	`P:variational-remove-mask`); both are smooth, in `[0,1]`, vanish near the
   467	endpoints and equal `1` on compact subsets of `(0,1)` for large `n`, which is
   468	all the proof uses. -/
   469	def cut (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   470	  Real.smoothTransition (((n : ℝ) + 4) * t - 1) *
   471	    Real.smoothTransition (((n : ℝ) + 4) * (1 - t) - 1)
   472	
   473	/-- `f_n = f_a · cut_n` (TeX lines 70-72, with the cutoff `cut_n`); `f_a` is
   474	`TemporalEquilibrium.density a`. -/

    18	  `H:homog` and `α < 2`, and a continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly

    90	  have key := integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable (μ := volume) (f := f)
    91	    (g := φ) (v := v)
    92	    ((hf1.continuous_fderiv one_ne_zero).clm_apply continuous_const |>.mul hφ1.continuous
    93	      |>.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hφ.2.mul_left)

   141	/-- **(F2)** For a nonzero measure with the set scaling of `H:homog`, every
   142	centred open ball of positive radius has positive mass. -/
   143	theorem measure_ball_pos {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hS : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   144	    (hΓ : Γ ≠ 0) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : 0 < Γ (ball (0 : Rd d) r) := by
   145	  have hex : ∃ n : ℕ, Γ (ball (0 : Rd d) ((n : ℝ) + 1)) ≠ 0 := by
   146	    by_contra h
   147	    push Not at h
   148	    apply hΓ
   149	    have hu : (Set.univ : Set (Rd d)) = ⋃ n : ℕ, ball (0 : Rd d) ((n : ℝ) + 1) := by
   150	      ext x
   151	      simp only [Set.mem_univ, Set.mem_iUnion, mem_ball, dist_zero_right, true_iff]
   152	      obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_nat_gt ‖x‖
   153	      exact ⟨n, by linarith⟩
   154	    have : Γ Set.univ = 0 := by
   155	      rw [hu]; exact measure_iUnion_null h
   156	    exact Measure.measure_univ_eq_zero.mp this
   157	  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := hex
   158	  set R : ℝ := (n : ℝ) + 1 with hR
   159	  have hRpos : 0 < R := by positivity
   160	  have hc : 0 < R / r := div_pos hRpos hr
   161	  have hball : (R / r) • ball (0 : Rd d) r = ball 0 R := by
   162	    rw [smul_ball hc.ne', smul_zero, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hc]
   163	    congr 1; field_simp
   164	  have := hS _ (measurableSet_ball (x := (0 : Rd d)) (ε := r)) (R / r) hc
   165	  rw [hball] at this
   166	  rw [this] at hn
   167	  exact pos_iff_ne_zero.mpr (right_ne_zero_of_mul hn)

   172	  (measure_ball_pos hS hΓ hr).trans_le (measure_mono ball_subset_closedBall)

    31	abbrev Rd (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)
    81	
    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`
    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=
    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩
    88	
    89	/-- `E:kappa` with the manuscript's hypothesis: under `H:homog`,
    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/
    91	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    92	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one
    95	    h.threshold h.alpha_range
    96	
    97	/-- `E:driver-parameters` with the manuscript's hypothesis (the section
    98	retains `H:homog` and sets `a = α₀`): its strict intervals are nonempty. -/
    99	theorem parameters_nonempty_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   100	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
   101	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
   102	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - alpha0 / 2) ((3 - alpha0 - alpha) / 2)) :=
   103	  DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty d alpha alpha0 (homog_params h)

   381	theorem exists_radius_fn {z : Rd d → ℝ} (hz : HasCompactSupport z) :

   398	/-- **(F1) The dilation floor.**  Let `Γ` be a nonzero locally finite measure
   399	on `ℝ^d` with the set scaling `Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)` of `H:homog`, and

   401	`y ↦ z(x - y)` `Γ`-integrable for every `x` (so `Γ * z` is a genuine
   402	integral).  Then there are a smooth compactly supported unit test `f`
   403	(`∫ f² = 1`), an `L²` weak gradient `g` of `f`, and `ε > 0` such that
   404	`ε ≤ ∫ V f² - ∫ ‖g‖²` for EVERY potential `V ≥ Γ * z` for which `V f²` is
   405	integrable.  The test is `f = U_ℓ φ / ‖φ‖₂` with a fixed bump `φ` and a
   406	small dilation parameter `ℓ`; the bound comes from
   407	`∫ V f² ≥ ℓ^α (∫ z) Γ(B̄₁)/‖φ‖₂²` (Tonelli in `(x, y)` and the scaling of
   408	`Γ` on balls) and `∫ ‖g‖² = ℓ² ‖∇φ‖₂²/‖φ‖₂²`, with `ℓ^α` dominating `ℓ²`

   411	theorem dilation_floor {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ]

   413	    {z : Rd d → ℝ} (hzc : Continuous z) (hzs : HasCompactSupport z) (hz0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ z x)

   418	        Integrable (fun x => V x * f x ^ 2) volume → ε ≤ rayleighValue V f g := by

   426	    have h2 : 0 < (Γ (closedBall (0 : Rd d) 1)).toReal :=

   432	  have hXpos : 0 < X := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (by positivity) _
   433	  set ℓ : ℝ := min (1 / (Rz + 1)) X with hℓdef
   434	  have hℓ : 0 < ℓ := lt_min (by positivity) hXpos
   435	  have hRℓ : ℓ * Rz ≤ 1 := by
   436	    have h1 : ℓ ≤ 1 / (Rz + 1) := min_le_left _ _
   437	    calc ℓ * Rz ≤ 1 / (Rz + 1) * Rz := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h1 hRz0
   438	      _ ≤ 1 := by rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, one_mul, div_le_one (by positivity)]; linarith
   439	  have hpow : ℓ ^ (2 - alpha) ≤ A / (B + 1) := by
   440	    have h1 : ℓ ^ (2 - alpha) ≤ X ^ (2 - alpha) :=
   441	      Real.rpow_le_rpow hℓ.le (min_le_right _ _) hk.le
   442	    rwa [hX, Real.rpow_inv_rpow (by positivity) hk.ne'] at h1

   444	    rw [← Real.rpow_add hℓ, ← Real.rpow_natCast]; congr 1; push_cast; ring

   447	    have hm : ℓ ^ (2 - alpha) * B ≤ A / (B + 1) * B := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hpow hB0
   448	    have hq : A / (B + 1) * B < A := by
   449	      rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_lt_iff₀ (by positivity)]; nlinarith
   450	    have hpa : 0 < ℓ ^ alpha := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hℓ _
   451	    rw [hε, hsplit]
   452	    nlinarith [mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (show ℓ ^ (2 - alpha) * B < A by linarith) hpa]
   453	  refine ⟨fl ℓ, gl ℓ, ε, hεpos, fl_test hℓ, memLp_test (fl_test hℓ), gl_memLp hℓ, gl_weak hℓ,

   456	  rw [rayleighValue, gl_norm hℓ]
   457	  have e : (profMass d)⁻¹ * ℓ ^ 2 * ∫ x, ‖grad (prof d) x‖ ^ 2 = ℓ ^ 2 * B := by
   458	    rw [hB]; ring
   459	  rw [e, hε]

   637	/-- **(F5) Zero weak gradient implies zero** (half (b) of the D8-lite
   638	foundation): for `d ≥ 1`, an `f ∈ L²(ℝ^d)` whose weak gradient is `0` is zero
   639	almost everywhere.  This is the fact used in `P:spatial-smooth-ratio`
   640	(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex`, lines 112-114 at 975feb3: "a nonzero
   641	`L²` function with zero weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported
   642	only at zero, and hence would vanish").  Lean proof route (different from the
   643	TeX's Fourier argument): the mollifications `ρ_n ⋆ f` are smooth with
   644	derivative `(Dρ_n) ⋆ f = 0` (`moll_const`), hence constant; they converge to
   645	`f` almost everywhere, so `f` is a.e. a constant `c`; and a nonzero constant
   646	is not in `L²(ℝ^d)` for `d ≥ 1` (infinite Lebesgue measure).  The hypothesis
   647	`d ≥ 1` is necessary: on `ℝ⁰` (one point) every function has weak gradient
   648	`0`. -/
   649	theorem ae_eq_zero_of_hasWeakGradient_zero (hd : 0 < d) {f : Rd d → ℝ}
   650	    (hf : MemLp f 2 volume) (h0 : HasWeakGradient f 0) : f =ᵐ[volume] 0 := by
   651	  have hloc : LocallyIntegrable f volume := hf.locallyIntegrable (by norm_num)
   652	  have hT := moll_tendsto f hloc
   653	  obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩ := hT.exists
   654	  have hconst : f =ᵐ[volume] fun _ => f x₀ := by
   655	    filter_upwards [hT] with x hx
   656	    have : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => moll f n x₀) Filter.atTop (nhds (f x)) := by
   657	      refine hx.congr fun n => ?_
   658	      exact moll_const hloc h0 n x x₀
   659	    exact tendsto_nhds_unique this hx₀
   660	  have hc : MemLp (fun _ : Rd d => f x₀) 2 volume := hf.ae_eq hconst
   661	  rw [memLp_const_iff (by norm_num) (by norm_num)] at hc
   662	  have : Nonempty (Fin d) := ⟨⟨0, hd⟩⟩
   663	  have htop : (volume : Measure (Rd d)) Set.univ = ⊤ :=
   664	    measure_univ_of_isAddLeftInvariant _
   665	  rcases hc with hc | hc
   666	  · filter_upwards [hconst] with x hx
   667	    rw [hx, hc]; rfl
   668	  · exact absurd hc (by rw [htop]; exact lt_irrefl _)

     1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision 975feb3, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98 and 3920258.
     9	The later revisions changed prose, titles, the literature review, layout and
    10	figures, added a zero-covariance remark after `H:homog` and qualified a strict
    11	comparison in `T:first` (not cited here) as asserted only for nonzero
    12	covariance. Every cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at
    13	3920258 and 975feb3. Between these two revisions every cited lemma,
    14	proposition, theorem and equation has the same statement and proof up to
    15	whitespace and braces, with one exception: the statement of `T:full-upper`
    16	(cited only as not formalized) now ends with a cross-reference to Theorem
    17	`T:intro-upper` instead of Goal `G:upper`, and its mathematics is unchanged.
    18	The cited sections `S:model` (the zero-covariance remark and a roadmap
    19	figure), `S:two-clock-screen` (Goal `G:sharp` renamed Theorem
    20	`T:intro-second-moment` in the prose), `S:temporal-equilibrium` and
    21	`S:intrinsic-white-evaluation` (new attribution paragraphs) changed only in
    22	prose. TeX line numbers were moved to 975feb3 by a line map; each cited range
    23	lies in unchanged text (script checks recorded in
    24	`provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    25	
    26	## Scope
    27	
    28	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    29	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    30	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    31	  elaborated types.
    32	- The rows cover every public theorem (1210) and 253 definitions whose
    33	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other
    34	  67 public definitions have no rows of their own: 63 (for example
    35	  `kappa`, `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`) only name quantities used in those
    36	  statements, and four are the instances that make `TimeCompletion.Pre` a
    37	  pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the Lean source or in
    38	  `Audit/`.
    39	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    40	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    41	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    42	  inner-product and finite-word facts.
    43	- The forty-seven `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked
    44	  "whole result" below; four of them are the wave-kernel and
    45	  time-fractional foundation of `ClockCopy`, `GaussianTest` is the

   167	  Parts of further results are formalized in wave L6, with named inputs
   168	  where stated: `P:variational-positive-scores` (everything except
   169	  `Q_2 >= S_2^pos`; the boundedness of the value sets and the supremum
   170	  statements rest on the named input `S1Bdd`, the proposition's own
   171	  boundedness claim at `c = 1`), `P:wave-two-variances` (the spectral core
   172	  in full; the statement for `E|l_R|^2` with
   173	  `E:variance-normalized-covariance`, the isometry `J` and the norm
   174	  identity of line 431 as named inputs), the finite Gaussian comparison of
   175	  `P:masked-noise-completion`, the facts about the wave Green measures
   176	  quoted in the proof of `L:higher-riesz`, and the scalar series bound in
   177	  the proof of `P:static-phase-all-orders`. Side conditions the TeX
   178	  leaves implicit (a probability
   179	  measure, integrability, measurability) are explicit hypotheses, and
   180	  integrability is part of each real-valued integral conclusion (extended
   181	  nonnegative integrals, such as the physical pairing of
   182	  `L:spatial-physical-pair`, need not be finite).
   183	- The SPDE itself, stochastic integrals, Gaussian measures (beyond finitely
   184	  many independent standard Gaussians, `GaussianIBP`, and the centered
   185	  Gaussian laws `N(0,A)` on `R^m` of the finite comparison in
   186	  `GaussianComparison`), Fourier analysis (beyond the Gaussian transform of
   187	  `P:masked-spectral-growth`, the auxiliary mask norm of
   188	  `P:masked-auxiliary-norm`, the wave-kernel and two-time Laplace
   189	  transforms, the Fourier transform of the `d = 1` wave Green measure
   190	  (`WaveGreen.waveGreen_fourier_one`), the spectral identity of
   191	  `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`P:masked-quotient-obstruction`) and the
   192	  spectral form of the autocorrelation integral in
   193	  `SpatialFourierBound`),
   194	  infinite-dimensional spectral analysis and operator theory (beyond the
   195	  finite-matrix results of `FiniteGaussianMatrix`) and limits in time or in a
   196	  regularization of the equation or its solution are outside Lean; the
   197	  scalar and norm-tail limits stated in their sections are formalized (for
   198	  example the tails `E:damped-tail-norms` and `K_M(r) -> 0` as
   199	  `M -> infinity` in `DampedNormsHomog`, and the limit of the decay bound of
   200	  `P:radius-mean-anchor` as `delta -> 0+`). Where a Lean statement needs an
   201	  analytic fact about the model, that fact enters as an explicit hypothesis
   202	  of the theorem (a "supplied hypothesis" below). Lean checks the deduction from
   203	  those hypotheses, not the hypotheses themselves.
   204	- A successful `lake build` is not a verification receipt for the
   205	  manuscript. It shows that the stated Lean theorems are proved from their
   206	  hypotheses; whether a statement matches the manuscript step it is listed
   207	  against is a separate, human judgment recorded in this ledger.
   208	- Three further modules developed alongside these (normalized Gaussian
   209	  coordinates, vector Gaussian projection, and colored vector words) are
   210	  withheld from this package because they depend on a library that is not

   213	  development of the manuscript that does not appear as, or inside, a
   214	  labeled statement of the revision cited above, or is a Lean-only
   215	  auxiliary or example (such as a non-vacuity instance) with no

    23	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian envelope for the original covariance]
    24	  \label{L:variational-heat-envelope}
    25	  For the normalized heat kernel $p_\epsilon(x) =
    26	  (2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/(2\epsilon)}$,
    27	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-heat-envelope}
    28	    (\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    29	    =\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}\mu(\ud\xi),
    30	    \qquad
    31	    0\le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    32	    \le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(0)<\infty.
    33	  \end{equation}
    34	  The value at zero is strictly positive.
    35	\end{lemma}
    36	
    37	\begin{proof}
    38	  A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial ball growth. Indeed, evaluate
    39	  its tempered bound on a nonnegative smooth cutoff equal to one on $B_1$,
    40	  dilated by $R \ge 1$. Its finitely many Schwartz seminorms are bounded by
    41	  $CR^N$, so positivity gives a ball-mass bound $CR^N$. Summing dyadic annuli
    42	  shows that $(1+|x|)^{-L}$ is integrable for $L > N$. Apply this separately to
    43	  $\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Gaussian weights are therefore integrable against both
    44	  measures. The classical convolution on the left is finite and smooth locally
    45	  in $x$: on compact $x$ sets its translated Gaussian derivatives are bounded by
    46	  any fixed sufficiently fast polynomial weight in the integration variable.
    47	
    48	  Pair the convolution with a Schwartz test $\varphi$. Absolute Fubini is
    49	  justified by these weights. The resulting pairing is that of $\Gamma$ with
    50	  $p_\epsilon*\varphi$. Applying the spectral convention in
    51	  Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} and the identity $\int p_\epsilon(y)e^{-i\xi\cdot
    52	  y}\ud y = e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}$ gives exactly the right side
    53	  of~\eqref{E:variational-heat-envelope} as a distribution. The heat kernel is
    54	  even, so either Fourier sign gives that same Gaussian multiplier. Its spectral
    55	  integral is absolutely finite and continuous in $x$ by dominated convergence.
    56	  Thus, equality of the two continuous distributions gives equality at every
    57	  $x$, without an extra normalization factor. The physical convolution is
    58	  nonnegative. Evenness of $\mu$ makes the spectral integral real, and its
    59	  absolute value is bounded by its total Gaussian mass, the value at zero.
    60	  Finally, $\Gamma \ne 0$ and $p_\epsilon > 0$ give strict positivity there.
    61	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope}.
    62	\end{proof}

    64	\begin{lemma}[Global regularity of the original mean]
    65	  \label{L:variational-global-mean}
    66	  Every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded in space,
    67	  uniformly on compact time intervals. In particular, for $I = [0,1]$ there are
    68	  finite constants $M,C_\Psi$ such that
    69	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-global-mean}
    70	    0\le h_s(x)\le M,\qquad
    71	    \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|,
    72	    \qquad s,t\in I.
    73	  \end{equation}
    74	\end{lemma}
    75	
    76	\begin{proof}
    77	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time; its compact support inside $(0,1)$ makes this a
    78	  smooth extension. For any mixed derivative $D\Psi$, a fixed $\epsilon > 0$ and
    79	  compactness of its common spatial support give $|D\Psi(t,x)| \le
    80	  C_Dp_\epsilon(x)$ for all $t,x$. Here the heat kernel has a positive minimum
    81	  on that support. Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope} consequently bounds
    82	  $\Gamma*|D\Psi(t,\cdot)|$ uniformly in $t,x$. Ordinary local differentiation
    83	  against the Radon measure gives the corresponding derivatives of the
    84	  convolution. After the change $r = s-t$,
    85	  \[
    86	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
    87	    (\Gamma*\Psi(s-r,\cdot))(x)\ud r.
    88	  \]
    89	  For $s$ in a compact interval the relevant $r$ lie in a fixed bounded
    90	  interval. The preceding global bound times $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable since $a <
    91	  1$. Every derivative thus falls on the smooth test and passes through the
    92	  integral by dominated convergence, with the claimed global spatial bounds.
    93	  Nonnegativity follows from positive kernels. The bounded time derivative
    94	  proves the Lipschitz estimate. No directional decay of the mean has been
    95	  inferred. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-global-mean}.
    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   102	  h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   103	  positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   104	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   105	    \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   106	    =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	  It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   110	  positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   111	\end{proposition}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  The Fourier Laplacian $A = -\Delta$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, being
   115	  multiplication by $|\xi|^2$ with its maximal domain. Multiplication $B_s =
   116	  -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is
   117	  densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
   118	  equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
   119	  \[
   120	    H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
   121	  \]
   122	  The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
   123	  1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
   124	  \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   125	  \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
   126	  $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
   127	
   128	  Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
   129	  Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
   130	  \[
   131	    \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
   132	    \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
   133	    \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
   134	  \]
   135	  Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(J_s)$ show that $H^2 = D(J_s)$ is a core for the
   136	  half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
   137	  equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
   138	  both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.
   139	
   140	  The spectral lower bound gives one direction of the Rayleigh identity. For the
   141	  reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
   142	  vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite
   143	  because the operator is bounded below and has finite Rayleigh tests. Let
   144	  $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Real tests give the same infimum: $q_s(u+iv) =
   145	  q_s(u)+q_s(v)$, so the quotient is the norm-weighted average of the nonzero
   146	  real quotients. This proves the Rayleigh identity with $-E_s$ on the left. The
   147	  following negative upper bound justifies writing that value as
   148	  $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2$ in~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}.
   149	
   150	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial} supplies, for this original
   151	  $\Psi$, one unit compactly supported $w$ and a finite plateau mask with a
   152	  common strictly negative upper bound $\epsilon_0 > 0$. Its trial has support
   153	  in $B_{2L}$; choose its plateau radius $R_0 \ge 2L$. The unmasked form on this
   154	  same $w$ is no larger. Consequently, $-M \le E_s \le -\epsilon_0 < 0$, and
   155	  $\sqrt{\epsilon_0} \le \lambda_{\Psi,s} \le \sqrt M$. Comparing identical unit

    13	\begin{lemma}[Gamma and Beta identities]\label{L:equilibrium-gamma-beta}

    27	  $R$; Tonelli gives the Beta--Gamma identity. For the last identity, symmetry,
    28	  then $t = (1+v)/2$ and $v^2 = w$, give $\operatorname{Beta}(x,x) =

    37	\begin{lemma}[Exact potential and mass]\label{L:temporal-equilibrium}
    38	  For $0 < a < 1$ put $r = (1-a)/2$ and, for $0 < t < 1$,

   398	\begin{lemma}[The original mean and variance]\label{L:compact-raw-profile}
   399	  Let $\Gamma \ne 0$ satisfy Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, let $a = \alpha_0$, and
   400	  let real nonnegative nonzero $\Psi \in C_c^\infty((0,1)\times\R^d)$ be
   401	  arbitrary, without a separability assumption. Define
   402	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-raw-mean}
   403	    h_\sigma(x)=\int_0^1|\sigma-u|^{-a}
   404	    (\Gamma*\Psi(u,\cdot))(x)\ud u,\qquad
   405	    \overline{q}(x)=\int_0^1\Psi(u,x)\ud u,\qquad Z=W(\Psi).
   406	  \end{equation}
   407	  Then $h$ is smooth in time and space on compact sets, and
   408	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-raw-cost}
   409	    0<v_\Psi:=\E Z^2
   410	    =\int_0^1\int\Psi(\sigma,x)h_\sigma(x)\ud x\ud\sigma<\infty.
   411	  \end{equation}
   412	  Against every smooth compact positive-time test $F_0$,
   413	  \[
   414	    \E[W(\Psi)W(F_0)]=\int F_0(s,x)h_s(x)\ud x\ud s.
   415	  \]
   416	  Moreover, on $I$,
   417	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-positive-mean-floor}
   418	    h_\sigma\ge\Gamma*\overline{q},\qquad
   419	    v_\Psi\ge Q(\overline{q})
   420	    :=\int\Gamma(\ud z)\int\overline{q}(x)\overline{q}(x-z)\ud x>0.
   421	  \end{equation}
   422	  For every fixed mask, $V_\sigma = m_Rh_\sigma$ is a smooth compact family,
   423	  Lipschitz in $\sigma$ in $L^\infty$ and $L^2$.
   424	\end{lemma}
   425	
   426	\begin{proof}
   427	  Choose $A \ge 1$ containing the spatial support of $\Psi$ in $B_A$. The
   428	  original covariance identity and absolute Fubini give the stated mean pairing:
   429	  the two compact tests restrict spatial differences to a compact set of finite
   430	  $\Gamma$ mass, and the time singularity is locally integrable since $a < 1$.
   431	  This identifies the linear covariance mean without evaluating noise at a
   432	  point. The same calculation gives~\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost}. Its spatial
   433	  integrand is bounded in integral by
   434	  $\|\Psi\|_\infty^2|B_A|\Gamma(\overline{B}_{2A})$, and
   435	  $\int_0^1\int_0^1|\sigma-u|^{-a}\ud u\ud\sigma = 2/((1-a)(2-a))$, proving
   436	  finiteness.
   437	
   438	  Nonnegative nonzero smooth $\Psi$ has positive integral, so $\overline{q} \ne
   439	  0$. Nonzero $\Gamma$ charges some ball, and homogeneity gives $\Gamma(B_1) =
   440	  r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(B_r) > 0$. Thus, every origin-centered ball $B_r$, $r > 0$,
   441	  has positive finite mass. The continuous compact autocorrelation
   442	  $\int\overline{q}(x)\overline{q}(x-z)\ud x$ is positive at zero and bounded
   443	  below on some ball. This proves $0 < Q(\overline{q}) < \infty$. Since
   444	  $|\sigma-u|^{-a} \ge 1$ on the unit time square, positive Tonelli gives both
   445	  inequalities in~\eqref{E:compact-positive-mean-floor}.
   446	
   447	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time and write
   448	  \[
   449	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
   450	    \int\Gamma(\ud z)\Psi(s-r,x-z)\ud r.
   451	  \]
   452	  On compact $s,x$ sets the relevant $r,z$ range over fixed compact sets;
   453	  $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable there. Every derivative falls on the smooth test, not
   454	  on the singular time kernel. Dominated differentiation gives smoothness and
   455	  continuity of all derivatives on compacts. Multiplication by $m_R$ now gives
   456	  the claimed compact family and its fixed-$R$ Lipschitz bounds. This proves
   457	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}.
   458	\end{proof}

   460	\begin{proposition}[Binding with the original control and cost fixed]
   461	  \label{P:compact-original-common-trial}
   462	  For every $\Psi$ in Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}, a sufficiently large
   463	  finite mask $m_R$ gives $V_\sigma = m_Rh_\sigma$ a common negative
   464	  trial~\eqref{E:compact-common-trial}. Thus, all preceding ground, projection,
   465	  positive-margin and complementary-wave conclusions apply. The rate is
   466	  Lipschitz on $I$ and has $\lambda_0 > 0$. The original test $\Psi$, original
   467	  variable $Z$ and variance $v_\Psi$ are unchanged by this choice. The mask can
   468	  additionally cover any fixed compact variational test supports.
   469	\end{proposition}

   471	\begin{proof}
   472	  Choose a real unit $L^2$ function $\psi \in C_c^\infty(B_2)$ with $\psi \ge
   473	  c_0 > 0$ on $B_1$, and put $\psi_L(x) = L^{-d/2}\psi(x/L)$, $D_\psi =

   476	  allowed real mask $0 \le m_R \le 1$, equal to one on $B_R$ and with support in

   481	    &\ge c_0^2L^{-d}\int_{B_L}(\Gamma*\overline{q})(x)\ud x\nonumber\\
   482	    &=c_0^2L^{-d}\int\overline{q}(y)\Gamma(B_L-y)\ud y\nonumber\\
   483	    &\ge c_0^2L^{-d}\Gamma(B_{L/2})\int\overline{q}

  4036	- (F1) `dilation_floor`, `rayleighSet_floor`: the dilation floor. For a
  4037	  nonzero locally finite `Gamma` with the set scaling
  4038	  `Gamma(c A) = c^(d-alpha) Gamma(A)` of `H:homog` and `alpha < 2`, and a

   270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies
   276	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-homogeneity}
   277	    S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}=c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}},
   278	    \qquad
   279	    Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}},
   280	  \end{equation}
   281	  where $Q_2$ is the original point liminf. The coefficient-one value is an
   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification
   283	  is asserted.
   284	\end{proposition}
   285	
   286	\begin{proof}
   287	  Write $k = 3-\alpha > 0$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $m = q/k > 1$. Fix one
   288	  $\Psi_0$ from the nonempty class and put $I_0 = I_{\Psi_0} > 0$, $v_0 =
   289	  v_{\Psi_0} > 0$. Positivity of the latter is
   290	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}. For $r_0 = (I_0/v_0)^{1/k} > 0$, which need
   291	  not be less than one, the exact real-power identity gives
   292	  \[
   293	    I_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}-v_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}/2
   294	    =r_0I_0-r_0^qv_0/2=r_0I_0/2>0.
   295	  \]
   296	  This positive value is obtained from a smooth nonnegative control.
   297	
   298	  For $c > 0$ put $r_c = c^{1/k}$ and $K_c = c^m > 0$.
   299	  Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation} and the exact scalar powers give,
   300	  for every $\Psi$,
   301	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-set-scaling}
   302	    cI_{D_{r_c}\Psi}-v_{D_{r_c}\Psi}/2
   303	    =K_c(I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2).
   304	  \end{equation}
   305	  Since $D_{r_c}$ is a bijection of the entire class, the whole set of
   306	  variational values with coefficient $c$ is $K_c$ times the whole
   307	  coefficient-one set of variational values.
   308	
   309	  We prove boundedness before taking finite-real suprema. The independent
   310	  Theorem~\ref{T:full-upper}, for the \emph{same canonical solution}, gives
   311	  \[
   312	    \E|u(T,0)|^2\le e(T+2)^d e^{C_{\mathrm{up}}T^\kappa},
   313	    \qquad T\ge1,\quad C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty.
   314	  \]
   315	  Its prefactor is negligible: choose $\epsilon = \kappa/2 > 0$, use $\log T \le
   316	  (T^\epsilon-1)/\epsilon$ and $\log(T+2) \le \log T+\log3$ for $T \ge 1$, and
   317	  divide by $T^\kappa$. Thus, the original point limsup is at most
   318	  $C_{\mathrm{up}}$. One fixed test/mask lower bound gives a finite lower bound
   319	  for $Q_2$, so $Q_2$ is finite. By~\eqref{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}
   320	  every coefficient-two variational expression is at most this same $Q_2 \le
   321	  C_{\mathrm{up}}$, uniformly in $\Psi$.
   322	  Equation~\eqref{E:variational-score-set-scaling} at $c = 2$ consequently
   323	  bounds all coefficient-one variational values by $C_{\mathrm{up}}/K_2$. The
   324	  nonempty set has a finite real supremum $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} > 0$ by the
   325	  positive test above.
   326	
   327	  For general $c$, set equality and $K_c > 0$ show that $K_cS_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   328	  is the supremum: it is an upper bound, and every smaller number is exceeded by
   329	  $K_c$ times a coefficient-one variational expression within the corresponding
   330	  positive distance of its supremum. This proves finiteness, positivity and the
   331	  first identity in~\eqref{E:variational-score-homogeneity}. Taking the
   332	  numerical supremum of the coefficient-two lower bounds proves the second.
   333	  Although $2^m > 2$, the resulting $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}} > 2S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   334	  is only a comparison of auxiliary variational values. It is not a Jensen
   335	  improvement without a first-moment identification. This proves
   336	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
   337	\end{proof}
